input.content: Anti-pattern: "simplifying" an ownership-guarded removal into an unconditional removal on shared keyed state. In cleanup_setup(store, workspace_id, setup_id), the guard `association = store.active.get(workspace_id); if association and association["setup_id"] == setup_id: store.active.pop(workspace_id, None)` was replaced by an unconditional `store.active.pop(workspace_id, None)`. The guard was an identity/ownership check ensuring the active slot is only cleared by the setup that owns it. Removing it causes a late/retried/superseded cleanup for an OLD setup_id to evict the CURRENT active association belonging to a DIFFERENT setup_id (lost-update / wrong-eviction correctness bug). Review heuristic: when a diff removes an `if owner == me` check before mutating shared keyed state (dict.pop, cache delete, map removal), treat the guard as load-bearing unless proven that the key always belongs to the caller at that point.
